correctness.rationale: Varvak's Corollary 1.3 gives a very general fiber isogenous to \(d\) pairwise non-isogenous Hodge-generic Abelian varieties of equal dimension \(g/d\), with \(d\mid g\). For the corresponding product Mumford--Tate group, Künneth degree two has one invariant in each exterior-square summand and none in cross tensor summands, so the rational degree-two Hodge-class space has dimension \(d\). Lefschetz \((1,1)\) identifies this with \(\operatorname{NS}\otimes\mathbf Q\), and isogeny preserves the rank. Proposition 2.8 realizes each factorization \(g=hd\) by a non-isotrivial symmetric-power construction, proving sharpness.

value.rationale: Picard number is a central discrete invariant of an Abelian fiber. The result gives a complete and sharp classification of that invariant for very general fibers in the non-isotrivial primitive-symplectic setting: not merely a bound, but exactly the divisor set of the fiber dimension. It also cleanly separates the closed-fiber Hodge invariant from Oguiso's scheme-generic arithmetic rank-one theorem and identifies where singular primitive-symplectic models enlarge the attainable behavior.
